templates.text: A line has gradient -[[m]] and passes through ([[a]], [[b]]). Find its equation and where it crosses the $y$-axis.
templates.answer: $y = -[[m|coef]]x + [[b + m * a]]$; crosses at (0, [[b + m * a]])

templates.subtopic: Equation of a straight line graph given one point and a gradient
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B2 Straight line graphs · S5 Equation of a straight line graph given one point and a gradient
templates.text: A line has gradient [[m]] and passes through ([[a]], [[b]]). Find its equation and the point where it crosses the $x$-axis. (3 marks)
templates.answer: $y = [[m|coef]]x[[b - m * a|signed]]$; crosses at ([[(m * a - b) / m|frac]], 0)

templates.subtopic: Real-life straight line graphs
templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B2 Straight line graphs · S10 Real-life straight line graphs
templates.text: A taxi charges a fixed fee plus a cost per mile: $C = [[f]] + [[m]]d$ where $C$ is in £ and $d$ in miles. What does [[m]] represent? What does [[f]] represent?
templates.answer: [[m]] is the cost per mile (the gradient); [[f]] is the fixed charge (the $y$-intercept)

templates.source: Y10 Higher Spring B2 Straight line graphs · S10 Real-life straight line graphs
templates.text: The graph shows the cost of hiring a bike: $C = [[f]] + [[m]]h$. (a) What does the gradient mean? (b) Why is the line not through the origin? (c) Work out the cost for [[h]] hours. (3 marks)
templates.answer: (a) £[[m]] per hour  (b) there is a £[[f]] fixed charge  (c) £[[f + m * h]]
